CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Payakumbuh.
2. Regional Government is the Government of the City of Payakumbuh.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Payakumbuh.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit within the Payakumbuh City Government.
5. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of protective, preventive, repressive or post-remedial (assistance and treatment).
6. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
7. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and Parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
8. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which are implemented with the approval and willingness of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
9. Child-Friendly Regency/City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency City that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
10. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old including a child who is still in the womb.
11. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, mentally, spiritually or socially.
12. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
13. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
14. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
15. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families and the community.
16. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Law enforcement is action by officials given authority by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
20. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
21. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence.
22. Shelter house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.
23. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
24. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
25. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
26. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, mother and her child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
27. Customs are eternal patterns of behavior passed down from generation to generation as heritage, so that they are strongly integrated with the behavioral patterns of society.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
1. GENERAL
Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty that we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor and rights as human beings that must be upheld. The human rights of children are part of human rights included in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.
As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves according to their abilities, dignity and honor.
As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and from acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the dignity of women themselves, women and children often become objects, outlets for desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect and so forth.
To realize the protection of women and children, support is needed, legislation that can guarantee its implementation.
The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Child Rights Convention, the government established Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the Rights of Children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, society, government and the State. Child protection in all its aspects is part of National development activities, particularly in advancing national and state life.
Parents, family and society are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.
Although the protection and rights of women and children have been regulated in national level legislation, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, then in providing Protection to women and children, the Payakumbuh City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children.

Article 50
(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services constitute actions by law enforcement apparatus to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

CHAPTER VI
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
First Part
Implementation of Protection for Women

PROTECTION
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Payakumbuh.
2. Regional Government is the Government of the City of Payakumbuh.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Payakumbuh.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit within the Payakumbuh City Government.
5. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of protective, preventive, repressive or post-remedial (assistance and treatment).
6. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
7. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and Parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
8. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which are implemented with the approval and willingness of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
9. Child-Friendly Regency/City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency City that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
10. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old including a child who is still in the womb.
11. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, mentally, spiritually or socially.
12. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
13. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
14. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
15. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families and the community.
16. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Law enforcement is action by officials given authority by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
20. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
21. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence.
22. Shelter house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.
23. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
24. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
25. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
26. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, mother and her child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
27. Customs are eternal patterns of behavior passed down from generation to generation as heritage, so that they are strongly integrated with the behavioral patterns of society.

Paragraph 1
Responsibility for the protection of Women.

Article 49
(1) Women and children victims of violence are provided with spiritual guidance aimed at psychological recovery.
(2) Spiritual guidance as intended in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. Not imposing any religion or belief; and b. Leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim/self determination) (3) Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guidance officers (4) Spiritual guidance officers as intended in paragraph (3) consist of Consultants from the Advisory, Development and Preservation of Marriage Agency (BP4), Officers from the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA), Ustad/Ulama, Pastors, Ministers and other religious leaders who are gender responsive

Article 43
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by Gender Responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and be able to empower victims.
Point b What is meant by Non-Discrimination is that every woman and child without exception has the right to receive services related to violence experienced, no one may be rejected or given priority over others except on the basis of certain emergency considerations.
Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relationships is that whoever the victim, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.
Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background and life experience so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any matter.
Point g What is meant by not judging is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.
Point h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken. Point i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and other backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in language understood by the victim. Lately there are increasingly more disabled/difable/disable women who become victims of violence, whether deaf, blind or those experiencing mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be drawn from special school (SLB) teachers.
Point j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without unnecessary delay. Perhaps several interventions require various parties, but with the proactiveness of service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.
Point k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.
Point l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and to participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Children. The Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Discrimination Against Women)

Article 42
The implementation of handling women and children victims of violence includes: a. Handling complaints of victims of violence.
b. Health services
c. Social rehabilitation
d. Enforcement and legal assistance, and
e. Repatriation and social reintegration.

6.8.rationale: The Indonesian regulation provides legal aid and protection in legal processes for victims and witnesses: Pasal 50(1) mentions providing protection for “saksi dan/atau korban,” and Pasal 51 details legal aid services including reporting/BAP, prosecution, court examination, mediation, and diversion, with a gender-responsive approach. This clearly involves victims/witnesses in legal processes. If the indicator ‘Legal process involvement’ under intersectionality is meant to capture something different (e.g., survivor participation/agency in proceedings, special procedural accommodations, or intersectional tailoring), the golden label ‘No’ may reflect that narrower construct. But based on the text, the judge’s Yes is supported; thus the disagreement most plausibly comes from the golden label definition/coding rather than lack of evidence.
